title: Power Apps: calendar and card layouts for views in model-driven apps
summary: The briefing passes: its status, targets and planned layouts agree with the roadmap. The documented environment path and CLI command are valid general controls, explicitly distinguished from the new layouts; targeted searches found no separate switch or layout-specific licensing.

claims.claim: No separate tenant or environment switch for the new calendar and card layouts was found on either the admin UI or API surface as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Apps" "new view layout" admin settings API; "calendar" "card" "layouts" "model-driven" enable admin API. Opened Manage feature settings, pac env and Organization reference; results describe existing calendar controls, not this new-layout switch.

claims.where: What's changing; front matter: confidence; Open questions
claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page specifically documenting these planned layouts was found, leaving feature-specific details dependent on the roadmap.
claims.quote: Searched: "575294"; "model-driven" "calendar" "card" "layouts" "designer". Opened Understand model-driven app views; read designer overview and Add the calendar control to tables excerpts. Existing calendar controls and mobile card forms do not identify this planned feature.

claims.claim: Detailed editing behaviour and available record actions for the new layouts are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "model-driven" "calendar" "card" "layouts" "designer"; "Power Apps" "new view layout" admin settings API. Opened Understand model-driven app views; read existing calendar-control excerpts, which do not establish actions for the planned layouts.

claims.claim: Existing table security applies to data accessed in model-driven apps.
claims.quote: Model-driven apps use role-based security for sharing. The fundamental concept in role-based security is that a security role contains privileges that define a set of actions that can be performed on tables within the app.

claims.claim: Existing column-level security continues to apply to data access.
claims.quote: Column-level security configurations are organization-wide and apply to all data access requests.
